quote.text: Some things are in our control and others not. Things in our control are opinion, pursuit, desire, aversion, and, in a word, whatever are our own actions. Things not in our control are body, property, reputation, command, and, in one word, whatever are not our own actions.
quote.author: Epictetus
quote.aiInsight:
• Parenthood
    • Recognize that while you cannot control every circumstance affecting your children, you possess the power to shape your reactions, choices, and the supportive environment you create.
    • Focus on nurturing virtues—patience, understanding, and love—instead of worrying about unpredictable outcomes; let your actions be guided by what is within your control.
  • Leadership
    • As a leader, concentrate on steering your actions, decisions, and integrity, while accepting that external factors like market fluctuations or team morale may not always be controllable.
    • By emphasizing self-discipline and clear communication, you empower your team to also focus on what they can manage, fostering resilience and accountability.
  • Product Management
    • In product management, concentrate on controlling the development process, quality, and innovation, while being prepared for unforeseen changes in market trends and user feedback.
    • Embrace challenges as opportunities to adjust your strategies, knowing that while external reception and circumstances vary, your clear vision and committed actions remain within your control.
